# Proposal: Practitioner Academy for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Client Profile and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has one deployed AI system (a customer service chatbot on the support portal), one in pilot (AI visual inspection on the German production line) and one planned for next year (AI sales forecasting). An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that no inventory of AI systems exists. The stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The EU AI Act and GDPR are the named regulatory drivers. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed. The Client names ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as incumbent frameworks. This proposal does not assume that any specific register, control or procedure exists under them. Where the program connects to them, the current state is `Unknown` until the Client confirms it.

## Why Hands-On Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The audit finding and the Q2 2027 production date both call for working artifacts rather than awareness training. Over two days, the Practitioner Academy has the Client's General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors build the first governance artifacts together inside the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Participants leave knowing where each artifact lives and how to continue the work without outside support. The program rests on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

## Running Worked Examples

- **Visual inspection pilot (primary).** This system is tied directly to the stated objective. It sits where quality, EU AI Act classification and the works council constraint meet.
- **Customer service chatbot (secondary).** This is the only deployed system. It tests the GDPR and EU data residency constraints and the design of escalation to a human.
- **Sales forecasting** enters the program only as a planned inventory entry, so that the inventory reflects all three systems.

**Confidentiality approach.** No customer data enters the exercises or the repositories. Chatbot exercises use synthetic support transcripts. Visual inspection exercises use synthetic defect descriptions and contain no information about production staff. All artifacts are drafts. The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff. Whether that consultation has begun is `Unknown`.

## Two-Day Curriculum Spine

The program is live and virtual. Each day consists of four 90-minute working sessions.

**Day 1: GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)**

| Session | Exercise | Module | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Telling of *The Turtle and the Phoenix* ([facilitation kit](https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md)), using the handle map as the bridge to the workbook. Participants then map the decision rights from visual inspection pilot to production, including the works council consultation step. | Governance structures | Draft decision-rights map, with owner names `Unknown` until confirmed |
| 2 | Enter the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting systems with their current status. Draft a preliminary EU AI Act classification rationale for legal review. | AI system inventories and classification | Started AI system inventory with three entries, responding to the June 2026 finding |
| 3 | Assess chatbot risks (data residency, GDPR, inaccurate answers) and visual inspection risks (false accept and false reject, possible effects on production staff). | Risk and impact assessments | Draft risk register entries and impact assessment outline |
| 4 | Draft an operating procedure for change control and use of visual inspection. Note interfaces with quality documentation, where these exist (`Unknown`). | Policies and operating procedures | Draft operating procedure |

**Day 2: Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) plus assurance**

| Session | Exercise | Pattern | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Write an Informed Intent statement and guardrails for the chatbot prompt, using synthetic transcripts. | Governed prompting | Governed prompt specification |
| 6 | Design the visual inspection workflow from image capture to disposition decision, with Slow AI checkpoints. | Practical AI workflow design | Governed workflow 1 |
| 7 | Design chatbot escalation to a human and the operator override for visual inspection, with a named accountable role for each. | Human oversight and accountability | Governed workflow 2 with oversight points |
| 8 | Define the evidence each artifact requires. The internal auditors act as reviewers, and participants apply acceptance criteria from The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done). Draft a board summary using AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). | Evidence collection and audit readiness | Evidence checklist, acceptance criteria and draft board summary |

## Deliverables

- A started AI system inventory covering all three systems.
- Draft risk register entries for the chatbot and the visual inspection pilot.
- At least two governed workflows: visual inspection disposition and chatbot escalation.
- A draft decision-rights map, operating procedure, governed prompt specification, evidence checklist and board summary.

These artifacts are a working foundation that the Client completes and owns. The program does not promise any certification or audit outcome, including for ISO/IEC 42001.

## Logistics and Price

- **Format:** two days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day.
- **Price:** US$12,500, within the stated budget of up to US$80,000 for this fiscal year.
- **Program dates:** `Unknown`, to be set after the decision.
- **Pre-work:** participants bring a list of the AI systems in their area, any existing policies and one live workflow they want governed.

## Next Step

The decision is expected by 15 December 2026. On approval, we will confirm program dates, issue the pre-work packet and agree the sanitized analog materials with the Client. Scheduling the program early in 2027 would leave time to finish the artifacts before the Q2 2027 production date.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: Session 8 lists "Evidence collection and audit readiness" under the Pattern column. That is a curriculum module name rather than a named repository file, and another scorer could call item 4 weakly met there. It does match the curriculum spine, and the session also names The Definition of Done and AI Governance for Boards with URLs, so I counted it as met.

The proposal says the Client's roles "build the first governance artifacts together" and that internal auditors "act as reviewers". I read both as proposed work drawn from AUDIENCE_ROLES, not as asserted Client facts.

Statements such as chatbot testing "the GDPR and EU data residency constraints" and the visual inspection system sitting where "the works council constraint" meets quality apply stated constraints to stated systems. Under the v1.14.3 guidance these are not new Client facts.

Incumbent frameworks are handled correctly. The proposal says "This proposal does not assume that any specific register, control or procedure exists" and renders the works council consultation status and quality documentation interfaces as `Unknown`.
The proposal is probably longer than the two pages the mode names. Page length is not in checklist items 1 to 7, so I did not score it.
